page.layout: One column of verse at the top, a woodcut divider, then a title with a drop-capped poem below. No marginal notes; faint show-through from the other side on the right edge is left out.

main_text.p: Mente simul iubet invocari Securiore : ut candida quæ tuis Semper relucet pollicitis fides, Hæc dicta firmet. Namque cuncta Sancte Deus potiore præstas. Promissa nutu. Nunc igitur tui Domum Davidis sollicitus vide Vultu benigno : splendidisque Auxiliis columnem tuere. Sic illa veris tuta favoribus Florens per urbes vivet Isacidum. Huic (te sereno) nulla posthac Sæcla ferent moribunda finem.
main_text.head: EX DECIMOQVARTO capite Esayæ.
main_text.p: CÆLO tonantis dextera Numinis Fastus superbos quum Babyloniæ, Cunctisque formidata regna Contudit: Atque trucem Tyrannū, (Qui sancta templi vasa Syonii Servire mensis iusserat ebriis, Sacrosque Iacobi cruentis Presserat Imperiis nepotes,) Fervente tandem Medus acynace

page.notes: The woodcut divider between the verse and the title is ornament, not text. The drop cap C is decorative and is joined to the first word as CÆLO. "Feruente" is read as "fervente" by the u/v rule. Doubtful: "Tyrannū" (tilde reading), "acynace" (final letter), and the letter after "Hæc", which may be "ac" without ligature. Printing errors are left as printed.
